notes: Round 10 runs several tracks at once, each in its own worktree: M1 (land animals), M2 (water mobs), M3 (night mobs) and W's w3 (the game events W's first merge left out). D0's d0b (silverfish in stone, endermites from pearls, flying navigation) is merged (c0366f3a), and release 6 is built with PROTOCOL 11 (789f6d23). Never bump minecraft_net::PROTOCOL: the release step bumps it once when messages changed; if a commit changes a ToClient/ToServer message or the codec, add a line under '## Protocol' in the track log. Insert new match arms and list entries next to related ones, not at the end of lists, to keep merges small (E3-0 names the few positional lists that are appended). Record decisions in the track log. LOAD: builds run at -j 4 per slot to keep the laptop cool; never start a second cargo command, the game, or any other long CPU-heavy process. Keep to the brief: each section names the commit its file:line anchors come from, so re-check every anchor before editing; keep off the hooks the M briefs own and follow the cross-area overlaps (both in E3-0). E2's e2b (44d96765) and D0's d0b (c0366f3a) are merged, so every 'waits for e2b', 'after d0b' and 'release 6 built' in the brief is met; d0b moved lines in server.rs, world.rs, walk_path.rs, entity_view.rs and families.rs, so anchors taken before it need a re-check. The orchestrator brings track-e3 up to minecraft-survival before each segment, so the review uses git diff r10-e3z-base..HEAD as usual. Track E3 group map-frames (last, optional): build track-e3.md section E3-14 group map-frames. Commits: 1. Minecraft maps in item frames mark their frame like vanilla. 2. Minecraft item frames show the map they hold, friends too. Key points: needs E2's e2b merged and group map-banners. (1) FrameView.map from the framed stack's minecraft:map_id (a '## Protocol' line). A typed MapFrame {pos, rotation, entity_id} in the codec's frames list. MapStore::tick_framed runs every 10 ticks per level (ServerEntity.sendChanges) and adds a FRAME marker under the key frame-<id> at rotation direction x 90, replacing a different frame at the same place. removed_from_frame runs when the map leaves the frame or the frame breaks. Framed map pictures go to the players who track the frame. (2) The world atlas reserves map slots; a framed map's picture (colours plus frame and banner markers, no player markers, no background) is written as an AtlasPatch when it changes. append_frames draws the map=true frame model and the picture with ItemFrameRenderer's transform: translate 0.4375, rotation % 4 x 90 degrees, rotZ 180, scale 1/128, translate -64 -64 then 0 0 -1; light 15728850 in a glow frame. The host uses Runtime.map_cache, a friend RemoteWorld.maps. If the atlas has no room, ship commit 1 alone and log commit 2 as left. The owner's steps and the kit line are in the brief.
